quest.title: Ending Note
quest.description: Amber says that Jean is waiting for you at the Cathedral. Apparently, it's something to do with the Holy Lyre der Himmel...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x375, Primogem x30, Mora x11325, Memory of Roving Gales x1, Adventurer's Experience x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x2

chapter.title: Song of the Dragon and Freedom

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This place is gonna collapse!

talks.objective: Meet Jean and Venti at the Cathedral

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: This is Barbara, the Deaconess of the Church. She is here to retrieve the Holy Lyre der Himmel.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: May the Anemo Archon protect you.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: I'm not really in a position to speak compared to our Acting Grand Master...

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: But I still want to thank you all on behalf of all of Mondstadt for your assistance!

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Fortunately, everything was resolved peacefully... I can't imagine how an all-out war between the military and the dragon would have ended...

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Now the Fatui have no choice but to keep their mouths shut.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: They must be annoyed that things didn't turn out as planned for them.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: This time, they even lost their best excuse to pressure the Knights of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Diplomatically speaking, they gained nothing, and on the contrary simply proved just how vexatious they can be.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Sounds like quite the story. So, did you bring the Holy Lyre with you?

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: We cannot ask you to keep defending the lyre forever. The Seneschal has been pressing me for a while now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We ahh... did bring it with us... Ummm... It's just... it's a little...

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry! I'm not here to collect rent! The Church has always received special funding...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: The wind amongst the branches is good, I love the way it smells...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Haha, I said the exact same thing the last time. *sigh* Why do I only say these things when I'm down on my luck?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So... what is a Gnosis?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ah, so you noticed.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: *sigh* This isn't something I'm meant to discuss with ordinary people. But I suppose I can let you in on the secret.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: As you know, Visions are external magical foci that only a small minority of people possess. They use these Visions to channel elemental power.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: In truth, every wielder of a Vision is one who can attain godhood and ascend to Celestia. We call such people allogenes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Allogenes? Paimon's never heard of them before.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's because this is a secret that only archons are privy to. We don't need primitive tools like Visions.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Instead, each archon has an internal magical focus that resonates directly with Celestia itself... known as a Gnosis.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about the thing hanging off your hip?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Eh-he. It's just a glowing glass ball I carry around to avoid suspicion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So who was that nasty woman who sent Paimon flying and stole your Gnosis?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Her name is Signora, No. 8 of the harbingers.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: She and the rest of the harbingers have been given god-like executive authority by the Tsaritsa of Snezhnaya, and with it, strength surpassing that of other mortals.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Tsaritsa of Snezhnaya? Isn't that...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Indeed. She is one of The Seven, the Tsaritsa who reigns from the Zapolyarny Palace, and the one person that the Fatui Harbingers all answer to.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The Seven don't always get along well, but still — I never thought that she would plot to steal another archon's Gnosis...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What sort of god is the Tsaritsa?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Ah... How should I put this?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Five hundred years ago, I knew her well. But I can't say the same is true now.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: You see, a certain catastrophe happened five hundred years ago, and after that, she cut off all ties with me.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But we can save discussion of the Cryo Archon and the Fatui for another day.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, if you seek the rest of The Seven, many difficulties lie ahead of you still.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: You should head for Mondstadt's neighboring nation of Liyue. The Geo Archon who reigns there, unlike me, administrates his entire region personally.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: He only descends once every year to give his divine predictions, which set the direction for Liyue for the rest of that year.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even so, it sounds like he works much harder than a certain someone.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Eh-he?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: ...In any case, this year's Rite of Descension is soon to begin. If you miss it, you'll just have to wait another year.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #WHAT!? Why didn't you tell us before? Well then bye. {NICKNAME}, we're going!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: One moment, Windborne Outlander.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Yup.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Traveler, as you set off on your journey once again, you must remember that the journey itself has meaning.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The birds of Teyvat, the songs and the cities, the Tsaritsa, her Fatui and the monsters... they are all part of your journey.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The destination is not everything. So before you reach the end, keep your eyes open. Use the chance to take in the world around you...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Great. So that's that for the Anemo Archon's admonishments! Back to Venti Time!

choices.text: Sorry for borrowing the statue's Anemo power without asking...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Haha, just use it gratefully — or, better yet, treat me to a glass of dandelion wine.

choices.text: I feel cheated... but I guess I'm used to that by now.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Ah! Honorary Knight, you're awake!

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: Um... I wouldn't say he's "alright," exactly.

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: I found you lying unconscious outside the Cathedral, and used my elemental powers to heal you...

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: That bard awakened first, but strangely, my healing powers had almost no effect on him...

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: This is the first time I've encountered such a patient. But he just said "it's completely normal," and then got up and left the Cathedral...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He left? Already? Where'd he go?

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: <color=#00E1FFFF>The Symbol of Mondstadt's Hero</color>, that's what he said.

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: I wanted to stop him, but Jean— I mean, Master Jean said to let him leave. How strange.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon remembers Venti healing under <color=#00E1FFFF>that tree</color> before...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (It's probably due to the connection between Windrise and the Anemo Archon. Master Jean has figured it out as well, but we can't tell Barbara...)

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: Planet?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Ah! Don't listen to {F#her}{M#his} nonsense, Miss Barbara!

response.speaker: Barbara
response.text: Ahh... Um, okay, well basically, I found you lying outside the Cathedral, unconscious, and used my elemental powers to heal you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks you could still use a final splash of ice-cold water to the face.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: If you want to chat, now's the time — a bard stays not always in a single clime.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Up till the end, Dvalin remembered his duty as one of the Four Winds.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: As such, I don't intend to forcibly strip him of that duty and force my ideals of freedom onto him.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I just hope that Dvalin will be able to choose for himself and understand what freedom is.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Before I became an archon, I too was taught the meaning of freedom in this way by a friend.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Kaeya shared some new intelligence, you say?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #...I see. So, the Abyss Order has a {F#Prince}{M#Princess} who orchestrated the plan to corrupt Dvalin?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #They were probably trying to turn Dvalin into a weapon of war for the Abyss. But that said, I have never heard of any such {F#Prince}{M#Princess} of the Abyss Order.

choices.text: Not an Abyss Order tradition, then.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I think so, too...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #Apparently, but how does a {F#Prince}{M#Princess} come out of nowhere and take command over the entire Abyss Order?

choices.text: So this is a recent development...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That Fatui lady didn't hang around, did she? She just grabbed your Gnosis and left!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: She wanted to avoid any eyewitnesses from the Knights of Favonius.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The slightest slip-up here would have destroyed the Fatui's diplomatic relations with the Knights.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So they're just gonna keep acting like Mondstadt's allies as if nothing happened!?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: *sigh*... If only the seven nations had banded together against the Abyss Order in the first place.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The Fatui possess the strongest military among the seven nations. Yet they've used it to steal the Holy Lyre, covet the power of gods, and use Dvalin as a bargaining chip against the Knights...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of the Lyre... didn't Diluc say something like this before?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He said that the Fatui can only run amok across the seven nations and threaten the Knights because of the harbingers.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Yes. As I said earlier, the Cryo Archon has given them authority and strength beyond that of other mortals.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The Tsaritsa... I haven't seen her in five hundred years. What is she thinking? What's her plan?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Whatever the answer is, I have a feeling it's only going to make your search for The Seven all the more difficult...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: As I said before, Vision wielders are known as allogenes and may ascend to Celestia.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: A Gnosis is a higher-order nexus of elemental manipulation and is emblematic of an archon's status as one of The Seven.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #But as for which of The Seven took your {F#brother}{M#sister}... I'm sorry, I don't know.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: ...Wait, as one of the Seven, I'm not clear of suspicion yet either, am I?

choices.text: You don't look like that god at all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hang on a hot second! Tone-Deaf Bard is just one of Barbatos' many incarnations, who's to say—

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We've known you long enough to trust you.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #Haha, we're a great team indeed! Say, once you find your {F#brother}{M#sister}, how would you like to become one of the new Four Winds?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Perhaps...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hmm, you don't seem too into it, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Tone-Deaf Bard... If being one of the Four Winds means free food, you can consider Paimon!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hahaha...

choices.text: We've known you long enough to trust you.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Well then, best be off to <color=#00E1FFFF>Liyue</color>. If the descension ritual you fail to tally, then another year you must dally.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: The Fatui were the ones who attacked you? That's too much...

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Master Jean has already returned to the Knights Headquarters. She said that she will look for evidence.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: But she also said that if no traces were left behind, the Knights might find it difficult to lodge a complaint against the culprit.
